items.question: Why does the yogi tremble when approaching the supreme?
premises: For hundreds of past births the yogi has been certain of identity with the body.
He imagines consciousness and body to be one like water and dust.
This ingrained identification resists the entry into the supreme.
items.inference: The trembling arises because long-established body-identification conflicts with the dissolution of the assumed unity of consciousness and body.
items.plain_english: He trembles because, for hundreds of past births, he has been certain of identity with the body and has imagined consciousness and body to be one, like water mixed with dust.
